Giving Your Senses a Rest

For anyone worn out by noise, bright light, screens and busy places. Each day is one small way to turn the world down a little, give your eyes, ears and attention a break, and plan calmer moments at home, at work and with people.

Rest · Stress · Self-Care · Burnout · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Dim the overhead lights an hour before bed and let one lamp carry the rest of the evening.
  • Day 2Turn your work screen brightness down a notch so it matches the light in the room around it.
  • Day 3Step outside a loud party for five quiet minutes, then go back in when you feel ready.
  • Day 4Change into the softest clothes you own as soon as you get home this evening.
  • Day 5Step outdoors after a snowfall and listen to how quiet the street has become.
  • Day 6Close the curtains as the sun sets and notice how the room feels once the glare is gone.
  • Day 7Switch off the sound for email and chat alerts on your work computer for the morning.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Take a slow walk with no podcast or music, letting the outdoor sounds be enough.
  • Day 60Count the different shades of green you can see on a walk after a spring rain.
  • Day 120Choose fewer decorations this season, letting a few soft lights be enough.
  • Day 240Eat breakfast on a park bench on a quiet fall morning, before the paths get busy.
  • Day 365Mark the holidays with one small, quiet ritual of your own, like a slow evening walk to see the neighbors' lights.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
